selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main comparison is used at the start of the passage to explain how different time periods relate to one another?
questions.answer: The passage compares them to the different hands of a clock, showing that smaller and larger cycles match, reflect, and follow one another.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the structure of the world by calling it a vast clock?
questions.answer: It suggests that the world runs in an ordered, measured, and purposeful way under Allah’s control.

questions.question: What does it mean that these layers are examples of one another?
questions.answer: It means they share patterns, so a person can understand one by reflecting on another.

questions.question: What is connected with days in this same pattern?
questions.answer: The long eras of the world’s life are connected with days.

questions.question: What is the broadest historical unit named in this section?
questions.answer: The great eras in the world’s lifetime.

questions.question: What general spiritual theme unites all the things associated with Fajr?
questions.answer: The theme of beginnings brought about by Allah.

questions.question: What stage of human beginning is linked with Fajr?
questions.answer: The beginning of life in the mother’s womb.

questions.question: Which prayer time is described as coming just after midday?
questions.answer: Zuhr.

questions.question: Which prayer time is connected with midsummer and the strength of youth?
questions.answer: Zuhr.

questions.question: Why does the passage begin with the image of a clock?
questions.answer: To show that time is arranged in connected layers, where one cycle can help explain another.

questions.question: Why is that object a helpful teaching tool in the passage?
questions.answer: Because its parts move in coordination, which helps explain how different time cycles are related.

questions.question: How is that same feature applied to the world?
questions.answer: The world’s daily, yearly, human, and historical cycles are shown as coordinated parts of one meaningful order.

questions.question: Name two beginnings that Fajr brings to mind.
questions.answer: It brings to mind early spring and the beginning of life in the womb.

questions.question: What broad historical dimension completes the pattern?
questions.answer: The major periods of the world’s existence.

questions.question: What human beginning is used to explain Fajr?
questions.answer: The earliest stage of life before birth.

questions.question: What age of life is associated with Zuhr?
questions.answer: The prime of youth.

questions.question: What period of a person’s life does Zuhr resemble?
questions.answer: The strongest and most developed part of youth.

questions.question: What does the passage highlight as being present in the realities connected with Zuhr?
questions.answer: Manifestations of mercy and many blessings.

questions.question: What idea does the passage communicate by saying the time cycles “look to” one another?
questions.answer: It means the cycles are linked in meaning, with each one reflecting and reminding us of the others.

questions.question: What are the four layers of time named in this section?
questions.answer: Daily cycles, yearly cycles, the phases of human life, and the long ages of the world.

questions.question: What part of human life is linked with hours in this pattern?
questions.answer: The stages of a person’s life are linked with hours.

questions.question: What everyday object is used to explain the connection between different kinds of time?
questions.answer: A clock.

questions.question: What feature of a clock is especially important in the opening comparison?
questions.answer: Its different hands move in relation to one another and represent different scales of time.

questions.question: How does the passage connect ordinary timekeeping with spiritual reflection?
questions.answer: It uses the structure of measured time to show that daily moments can point to greater realities created by Allah.
